ETag.description: Fingerprint of the new connection. Same value as eTag in the body; send it as If-Match on later replace or delete calls.

400.description: Bad Request. The body was invalid; issues explains why.

post.description:
Creates a tenant-scoped connection after validating category + provider + authMode + settings as one consistent unit against the provider catalogue (GET /api/v10/Connections/catalogue).

Mind map - how the fields lock together (enums are sent as string names, picked from the dropdown):
1. provider must exist in the catalogue (e.g. "Oracle"), else error provider.unknown.
2. category must equal that provider's category (Oracle lives in "Database" only), else provider.category.
3. authMode must be one the provider supports (Oracle: "ConnectionString", "Basic", "BearerToken"), else provider.authMode.
4. settings/secretSettings may only use keys from (provider required+optional keys UNION auth-mode keys); unknown keys are rejected (setting.unknown). Max 128 entries each.
5. Required gates: provider required public keys in settings (Oracle: host, database), required secret groups for the auth mode ("Basic" needs username AND password).

Oracle example (Basic auth): category="Database", provider="Oracle", authMode="Basic", settings={"host":"...","database":"...","port":"1521"}, secretSettings={"username":"...","password":"..."}. Secrets are encrypted at rest and never returned; the 201 response echoes public settings only, plus id, revision=1, eTag, audit fields, reconnectRequired and capabilities.

ConnectionAuthMode.description: Credential strategy, returned as a number (e.g. 4 = Basic).

supportsTest.description: True if the Test endpoint can run a live connection check for this provider. Currently only Sqlite supports it.

supportsSchemaDiscovery.description: True if the schema endpoints can list this connection's tables. Currently only Database + Sqlite supports it.

ConnectionCategory.description: Capability group, returned as a number (e.g. 0 = Database).

ConnectionProvider.description: Concrete system, returned as a number (e.g. 3 = Oracle).

id.description: ID of the new connection. Save it: every later get, replace, delete or test call needs it.

name.description: The name you sent. Shown in pickers and dropdowns.

authMode.description: The sign-in method that was accepted.

settings.description: The public settings you sent, echoed back (host, database, port and so on).

revision.description: Version number of the connection. It is 1 when created and increases each time it is replaced.

eTag.description: Fingerprint of this version. Send it back as If-Match when you replace or delete the connection. Also returned in the ETag header.

createdBy.description: ID of the user who created the connection.

updatedBy.description: ID of the user who last replaced the connection. Null until the first replace.

updatedOn.description: When the connection was last replaced (UTC). Null until the first replace.

reconnectRequired.description: True when the saved OAuth sign-in has expired and the user must authorize again.

capabilities.description: What you can do with this connection.

ConnectionSummary.description: The connection that was created. Secrets are never included, only public settings.

name.description: A friendly name for the connection, such as "Analytics Postgres (prod)". Up to 256 characters.

category.description: The type of system you are connecting to. Must match the provider. Pick from the dropdown (sent as a string, e.g. "Database").

provider.description: The exact system to connect to. Pick from the dropdown (sent as a string, e.g. "Oracle").

authMode.description: How the connection signs in. Each provider supports only some modes. Pick from the dropdown (sent as a string, e.g. "Basic").

settings.description: Non-secret details such as host, database or port. Every value is text, even numbers. Use only the keys listed for your provider in the catalogue.

secretSettings.description: Sensitive details such as a username, password or API key. They are stored encrypted and are never shown again. Use only the keys your sign-in method needs.

CreateConnectionRequest.description: Details of the connection to create.

ConnectionValidationResult.description: Returned when the request fails validation. Nothing was created.

isValid.description: False means the request was rejected. Fix the issues below and try again.

issues.description: One entry for each rule that failed, such as a missing setting, an unknown key or a provider and category that do not match.

code.description: Short ID of the rule that failed, for example name.invalid, provider.unknown, provider.category, provider.authMode, setting.required, secret.required, setting.unknown, setting.value.limit, setting.value.invalid or setting.port.invalid.

message.description: Plain-language explanation, for example "Required setting 'host' is missing." Safe to show to a user.

severity.description: How serious the issue is. Always Error here.

settingKey.description: The settings or secretSettings key that caused the error, such as host. Null for whole-request errors like an invalid name.
